BMW M 100 Jahre Nürburgring Edition That Marks 100 Years of Green Hell Also Comes to Australia
36 photos
Photo: BMW
The global BMW M “100 Jahre Nürburgring” Edition celebrates 100 years of legendary German track prowess, and fans in the Land Down Under get in on the action, though only partially.
Back in early September 2026, the premium German carmaker BMW announced a collection of nine cars and motorcycles tasked with one singular goal: celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Nürburgring track in Germany. The little town in Germany called Nurburg got its racetrack opened in 1927, and at the time probably nobody thought that the racing circuit, officially called the Nürburgring , would turn out to evolve into one of the most important pieces of asphalt and racing track elements in global automotive history.
Everyone comes here to test all the newest automobiles and technologies, at the same time competing against each other in a well-known yet undeclared war of hubris, trying to achieve the best lap times across the 13-mile (almost 21 km) version of the track known as the Nordschleife or the Green Hell. One German automaker, in particular, moved to obliterate the competition with its tribute to the track: BMW decided to celebrate the anniversary with no less than nine special vehicles with both two and four wheels.
More precisely, the fleet consists of six BMW M cars and three BMW Motorrad M motorcycles, all painted in Nürburgring Green and sporting Nordschleife motifs: M2, M3 sedan and Touring, M4 Coupe, plus the M5 sedan and Touring. The bikes, on the other hand, are the BMW M 1000 RR, M 1000 R, and M 1000 XR. How about Australia?
Well, the local division of BMW happily announced in early November 2026 that four models from the global roster have also been confirmed for the Land Down Under: BMW M2 xDrive, M3 Competition Sedan M xDrive, M4 Competition Coupe M xDrive, and the M5 Sedan. BMW M calls this gathering the exclusive “100 Jahre Nürburgring” edition, and only a very limited number of cars will make the trip to Australia in right-hand-drive form.
Yup, you need to hurry to snatch one of these special editions, as only 16 automobiles have been reserved for Australia . Pricing starts from AU$155,800 MRLP including GST and LCT, which is about $109k at the current exchange rate. BMW says Australia is a growing market for the M division, with almost 10% of the global sales of 2025 and 20% of the brand’s overall sales from January through September 2026.
All versions of the special edition wear the special BMW Individual Nürburgring Green paint finish on the outside, but there’s also an alternate mod in Black Sapphire metallic if anyone wants it. The most expensive option is the M5 Sedan, of course, which starts at no less than AU$280,800, which is the equivalent of more than $196k at the current exchange rate.
